title: PRICE: 945 of 945 on a fresh held-out gate, 14 extreme-yield rows still open
status_plain: PRICE has the cleanest held-out gate in the bond domain: battery b38, five new bonds covering month-end, leap, n=1 and extreme-yield cases, 945 of 945 across all five bases, re-run and reproduced independently by the coordinator. That figure is genuinely fresh -- the source's own words are fresh, held-out and 5 new bonds. Beside it sits the identification battery b37 at 7,458 of 7,472, which is the fitted corpus and must not be described as held out. Two earlier PRICE figures on this row are superseded and are recorded as such: 56 of 90, which was the sign-off sweep that found the Actual/360 and Actual/365 blocker, and 25 of 25 on the on-coupon binexp ladder before that blocker was known. Fourteen extreme-yield rows remain open.

substrate: Excel's PRICE derives the settlement discount fraction by the universal rule dsc = E − A rather than counting days from settlement to the next coupon; the fractional discount power is the x87 CRT chain exp(RN53(RN64(y·ln x))) (`excel_pow_chain`), the integer power is binary exponentiation (`excel_bond_pow`), and the body is plain single-rounded double with coupons ascending and a separate redemption term

substrate_bands.fingerprint: the C-runtime pow integer special case, i.e. binary exponentiation, not Rust powf's exp-times-ln

substrate_bands.band: fractional discount exponents, all five bases
substrate_bands.fingerprint: dsc = E − A plus the x87 CRT pow chain, the same pow identified in the G3 lane-1 distribution substrate
Excel's published value is up to +3 ULP above the correctly-rounded true sum, described as an accumulation op-graph fact

ruled_out: Rust's `base.powf` for integer exponents: it computes exp times ln even for integers, where Excel uses the C-runtime pow integer special case
counting days from settlement to the next coupon directly: Excel never does, it derives dsc = E − A universally
an x87 double-rounded body, an extended accumulator, and eight summation orders (`agentV_results.md`)
